transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-05-30
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Sara Patel (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Karen Liu (CTO, Aurora), Marcus Hale (Platform Eng), Dina Park (Security), Evan Ross (Product)

Auto-summary: Short demo of Redwood rate limiting and multi-tenant org/project key model. Walkthrough of Console settings, per-route limits, quotas, and emergency throttling. Discussed compliance and private deployments for regulated PHI workloads.

[00:00] Sara (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Sara, AE at Redwood, and Diego is our SE who will drive the demo. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Karen (Aurora): Hey Sara, Karen here. Marcus, Dina, Evan in the room with me.
[00:10] Diego (Redwood): Great, will share my screen, jumping into the Console. Apologies if the audio is a bit fuzzy, connection is fine on my end.
[00:20] Marcus: No problem. Curious high level — we want to understand how rate limits and quotas map to our multi-tenant model. We use org-level billing and project or client-level keys today.
[00:30] Sara: Perfect, that's exactly what we'll show — org keys, project keys, per-route limits, and how to do soft and hard quotas. Also how to do burst windows and token vs request-based limits.
[00:40] Diego: Okay sharing, Console > Organizations. So here's Aurora's org (demo data). We have projects under the org — web-portal, analytics, and partner-integrations. Each project gets its own project key which you can rotate independently.
[01:05] Diego: (narration) The org key is primarily for admin tooling and billing, project keys are scoped for client usage and RBAC. You can attach a quota to either: per-project monthly token cap, or per-route requests/sec.
[01:25] Dina (Security): Quick q: if we rotate a project key, does that invalidate in-flight sessions or cached tokens? We use some long-lived sessions for background jobs.
[01:35] Diego: Good question. Rotating a key issues a new key immediately; in-flight requests with the old key are permitted for a configurable grace period default 5 minutes. We also recommend using short-lived deploy tokens for jobs. The transcript may say 'five' or '50' it's five minutes - sorry for mis-speak.
[01:55] Evan: How do we enforce per-customer quotas? Our tenants vary a lot — some hit burst traffic.
[02:05] Sara: You can set per-project quotas and then create a per-route policy to cap a specific API endpoint. We also support tagging requests (customer_id header) and applying a secondary rate limit via policy engine — so you can do global org SLO and per-tenant limits.
[02:25] Marcus: That tagging — is it automatic or do we have to set it in our proxy?
[02:30] Diego: You'd add a header or claim in JWT; Redwood supports parsing header/jwt claims for routing and quota keys. We have examples in the docs — link: https://app.redwood.ai/docs/org-keys (note: demo link).
[02:50] Karen: On enforcement — is rate limiting client-side or server-side? We need hard guarantees for prod.
[02:55] Diego: Server-side enforcement. All requests hit our edge that applies limits — we enforce both token-bucket and leaky-bucket variants, you can choose strict rejection or soft-throttling (429 vs queued with retry-after). For Dedicated deployments it's identical from API perspective; enforcement still happens at the chosen ingress.
[03:20] Dina: For PHI workloads, we may go Dedicated/on-prem. Does the console still show those metrics?
[03:28] Sara: Yes, for Private/Dedicated we provide a control plane that can be hosted privately or integrated with your VPC. You still get the same console UX or a private console instance; audit logs and metrics ship to your chosen destination.
[03:40] Dina: KMS question — if we use our KMS, does Redwood manage keys?
[03:45] Diego: We integrate with customer KMS/HSMs. Keys for encryption at rest and key wrapping can be either Redwood-managed or customer-managed. When customer KMS is enabled, logs show key identifiers but payloads are inaccessible to Redwood. We'll follow up with the KMS integration checklist.
[04:10] Sara: Alright Diego, can you demo rate limit policies?
[04:15] Diego: Sure — Console Policies > Rate Limits. Create new policy: name, scope (org/project/route), limit type (requests/sec or tokens/minute), burst window, enforcement type. (narration) I'm creating a project-level policy: web-portal, 100 req/sec with a burst of 300 for 60 seconds and a monthly token cap of 2M tokens.
[04:50] [screen action noise]
[05:00] Diego: You can also pin policies to routes like /generate or /embeddings, and set different enforcement for streaming endpoints.
[05:20] Marcus: For embeddings we generally use large batch calls — can we set token-based quotas for embeddings separately?
[05:25] Diego: Yes, token-based quotas are supported and you can exclude certain internal service accounts from quotas, e.g., system-ops can bypass.
[05:40] Karen: How do alerts work? We need to know when tenants approach quota.
[05:45] Sara: Alerts feed into the Console and can be pushed to PagerDuty/Slack. You get near-capacity warnings and automatic throttling actions; you can also trigger webhook hooks for custom workflows.
[06:05] Dina: Audit log granularity — do we get per-request metadata? Retention?
[06:10] Diego: Audit logs include request metadata (timestamp, key, route, decision code, tokens consumed). Retention is configurable depending on plan. For enterprise we support 12+ months and archive to your S3.
[06:30] Karen: Any limits on number of projects or keys? We run a lot of internal projects.
[06:35] Sara: No hard limit; we can support thousands of projects. There's a pagination model in the API for key listing.
[06:45] Evan: What about emergency global throttles during incidents?
[06:50] Diego: We have an emergency throttle toggle at org level — you can enable global fallback to a low-cost model or give priority routing to critical projects. Also automatic fallback to compatible model variants if capacity is constrained.
[07:10] Marcus: Can policies be templated or applied via IaC?
[07:15] Diego: Yes, full policy CRUD via API and Terraform provider sample is in the docs. You can template policy sets per environment.
[07:30] [Diego starts quick live test]
[07:40] Diego: I'll run a quick synthetic load against the /generate route to show enforcement. Starting load test now.
[07:50] [short pause, load test sounds; transcript shows automated lines] 
[08:20] Diego: We hit the project limit — you can see 429s being issued for that project. Console shows real-time rate-limit metrics and a heatmap by route.
[08:40] Karen: That looks good. Any possibility to allow short bursts above quota for verified partners?
[08:45] Diego: You can create allowlist policies for specific project keys or tags — those keys get a different bucket.
[08:55] Dina: About token accounting — do stream tokens count the same as non-stream tokens? We saw differences earlier with other vendors.
[09:05] Diego: We count tokens consumed by the model regardless of streaming. Streaming just controls the output delivery, but tokens are accounted when generated. There is a small rounding effect sometimes due to sub-tokenization but it's consistent.
[09:25] Evan: Ok, on pricing, is there overage billing or enforced cutoffs?
[09:30] Sara: Both options. For hosted you can choose soft overage billing with alerts or hard cutoffs. For Dedicated reserved capacity is preferred to avoid surprise overages. We can show pricing examples in the follow-up email.
[09:50] Karen: Interested in a short pilot — maybe start hosted for low-risk pipelines and target Dedicated for PHI pipelines. Timeline wise, we'd like to pilot in June.
[09:58] Sara: Sounds great. We'll set up a small benchmark and a security deep-dive. Diego, any notes on the benchmark specs?
[10:05] Diego: We'll run a 30k-token mixed workload: 30% embeddings, 50% chat/generate, 20% rerank. We'll compare latency/cost hosted vs small-dedicated pool and share CSV.
[10:22] [brief cross-talk]
[10:30] Marcus: One more — how are quotas represented in the API response? We want to surface usage to our front-end.
[10:35] Diego: The response headers include X-Org-Remaining-Tokens and X-Project-Remaining-Tokens; you can also poll usage endpoints for more detail.
[10:45] Dina: SSO/SAML piece — can admin roles be scoped per-project? We need least privilege for auditors.
[10:50] Sara: Yes, RBAC supports org admin, project admin, project viewer roles. You can map SAML groups to roles.
[11:05] Karen: Anything else re compliance? SOC2 scope?
[11:10] Diego: We have SOC 2 in our security pack; we'll send the security whitepaper and SOC 2 summary. For PHI workflows we recommend Dedicated + VPC + customer KMS.
[11:25] Sara: Ok let's recap next steps — we'll send docs and pricing, Diego will run benchmark, and we'll schedule security deep-dive.
[11:35] Karen: Thanks, that's helpful. We'll confirm stakeholders and get back with pilot users.
[11:40] Sara: Bye everyone.
